## Parameters file
Demultiplexing was a difficult task, because of how disorganized the
original data was. After demultiplexing, it was necessary to merge the
individually demultiplexed projects and to branch out only the
*Crepidostomum* samples (it turns out they were not alone). Here, my
intention was to run clustering (step 3) and subsequent steps from the
already filtered and trimmed reads of only *Crepidostomum* samples,
present in `../2023-05-17/crepi_edits`. However, I realize that a reason
for this not to work is that `ipyrad` will not run step 3 unless step 2
is already done. And I cannot tell `ipyrad` I did that in another folder,
because `ipyrad` trusts the `crepi.json` file, which contains the whole
history of the analysis.

Thus, if I am to run steps 3 on in a different folder from where steps 1
and 2 were run, I need to hack the `ipyrad.json` file, for which I need
to bring some files here...

```{bash param}
if [ ! -d crepi_edits ]; then
   # Hard links not allowed for directories
   mkdir crepi_edits
fi
for f in $(ls -1 /nata/mar/crepidostomum2/results/2023-05-17/crepi_edits); do
   if [ ! -e crepi_edits/$f ]; then
      ln /nata/mar/crepidostomum2/results/2023-05-17/crepi_edits/$f crepi_edits/$f
   fi
done

if [ ! -e crepi.json ]; then
   JSON=/nata/mar/crepidostomum2/results/2023-05-17/crepi.json
   sed 's|/nata/mar/crepidostomum2/results/2023-05-17|../2023-05-17b|g' $JSON | \
   sed 's|Merged: PAR2no10, PAR2no11, PAR2no12, PAR2no13, PAR2no14, PAR2no15, PAR2no16, PAR2no1, PAR2no2, PAR2no3, PAR2no4, PAR2no5, PAR2no6, PAR2no7, PAR2no8, PAR2no9||g' \
   > crepi.json
fi

if [ ! -e ipopmap.txt ]; then
   cp ../2023-05-17/ipopmap.txt ./
fi

if [ ! -e params-crepi.txt ]; then
   PARAMS=/nata/mar/crepidostomum2/results/2023-05-17/params-crepi.txt
   sed 's|/nata/mar/crepidostomum2/results/2023-05-17|../2023-05-17b|g' $PARAMS | \
   sed 's|Merged: PAR2no10, PAR2no11, PAR2no12, PAR2no13, PAR2no14, PAR2no15, PAR2no16, PAR2no1, PAR2no2, PAR2no3, PAR2no4, PAR2no5, PAR2no6, PAR2no7, PAR2no8, PAR2no9||g' \
   > params-crepi.txt
fi

IPYRAD=/opt/miniconda3/envs/ipyrad/bin/ipyrad
for i in 85 90 92 94 96 98; do
   if [ ! -e params-crepi$i.txt ]; then
      $IPYRAD -p params-crepi.txt -b crepi$i
      sed -i "/## \[5\]/c denovo          ## [5] [assembly_method]"         params-crepi$i.txt
      sed -i "/## \[14\]/c 0.$i           ## [14] [clust_threshold]"        params-crepi$i.txt
   fi
done
```

The successful branching above suggests that I convinced `ipyrad` to use the
edits from the previous *crepi* run here in this new folder. I only had to
update the paths. And I erased the information of the previous merging. Unfortunately,
this is not portable, and I had to transfer all `json` and `params` files to
Garnatxa and edit them there again. I am not keeping copies of those files, but
I will save here the submission files at least.

## Step 3: within sample clustering
Running `ipyrad` from within an Rmarkdown document is not easy,
because `bash` blocks start a `bash` session in a new environment,
not in the same conda environment where we may be executing the
Rmarkdown document. In addition, I plan to run `ipyrad` in Garnatxa.
Actually, the submission scripts must be saved here. Below I transcribe
the commands as if they were run here, but they are not.

```{bash clustering, eval=FALSE}
for i in 85 90 92 94 96 98; do
   if [ ! -e clustering0.$i.log ]; then
      ipyrad -p params-crepi$i.txt -f -s 3 -c 6 1> clustering0.$i.log 2> clustering0.$i.err &
   fi
done
wait
```

The six processes shown above run for 24 hours in Garnatxa, and most of them
finished. Even incomplete runs are useful to compare the clustering efficiency
among clustering thresholds. I only need the clusters from at least one sample
to get an idea of how the number and size of clusters change with the threshold.

```{bash checkClusters}
if [ ! -e summary_clustering.txt ]; then
   echo -e "Sample\tClustThres\tClustNum\tMeanSize" > summary_clustering.txt
   for s in N044Cx2 S004Cmb S023Cxc S027Cxa S117Cmb S125Cma S125Cmc; do
      for i in 85 90 92 94 96 98; do
         gawk -v SAMPLE=$s -v CLUST=$i '(/^\/\//){
            N += 0.5
            if (S > 0) F[S]++
            S = 0
         }(/^>/){
            split($1, A, /;/)
            split(A[2], B, /=/)
            S += B[2]
         }END{
            HISTOFILE = FILENAME
            gsub(/clust\.txt/, "histo.txt", HISTOFILE)
            N += 1
            F[S]++
            for (s in F) {
               SUMSIZE += F[s] * s
               SUMFREQ += F[s]
               print s "\t" F[s] >HISTOFILE
            }
            if (N != SUMFREQ) exit "Error counting?"
            print SAMPLE "\t" CLUST / 100 "\t" N "\t" SUMSIZE / SUMFREQ
         }' crepi${i}_clust_0.$(echo $i | sed 's/0$//')/$s.clust.txt >> summary_clustering.txt
      done
   done
fi
```

```{r clusterPlots}
library(ggplot2)
clusters <- read.table('summary_clustering.txt', header = TRUE)
ggplot(clusters, aes(x = ClustThres, y = MeanSize, color = Sample)) +
   geom_line() + geom_point() + xlab('Clustering threshold') +
   ylab('Average cluster size')
ggplot(clusters, aes(x = ClustThres, y = ClustNum, color = Sample)) +
   geom_line() + geom_point() + xlab('Clustering threshold') +
   ylab('Number of clusters')
```

```{r fullDistribution}
library(MetBrewer)
N044Cx2 <- lapply(c(85, 90, 92, 94, 96, 98), function(x) {

# Order by decreasing cluster size and add cumulative sum
N044Cx2 <- lapply(N044Cx2, function(x) {
   z <- x[order(x$Size, decreasing = TRUE),]
   z$CumFreq <- cumsum(z$Freq)
   z$CumSum <- cumsum(z$Size * z$Freq)
   return(z)})
S004Cmb <- lapply(S004Cmb, function(x) {
   z <- x[order(x$Size, decreasing = TRUE),]
   z$CumFreq <- cumsum(z$Freq)
   z$CumSum <- cumsum(z$Size * z$Freq)
   return(z)})
S023Cxc <- lapply(S023Cxc, function(x) {
   z <- x[order(x$Size, decreasing = TRUE),]
   z$CumFreq <- cumsum(z$Freq)
   z$CumSum <- cumsum(z$Size * z$Freq)
   return(z)})
S027Cxa <- lapply(S027Cxa, function(x) {

S117Cmb <- lapply(S117Cmb, function(x) {

S125Cmc <- lapply(S125Cmc, function(x) {

   z$CumSum <- cumsum(z$Size * z$Freq)
   return(z)})

# N50
N044Cx2.N50 <- sapply(N044Cx2, function(x) {
   HalfNumReads <- max(x$CumSum) / 2
   k <- min(which(x$CumSum >= HalfNumReads))
   N50 <- x[k, 'Size']
   return(N50)
})
S004Cmb.N50 <- sapply(S004Cmb, function(x) {
   HalfNumReads <- max(x$CumSum) / 2
   k <- min(which(x$CumSum >= HalfNumReads))
   N50 <- x[k, 'Size']
   return(N50)
})
S023Cxc.N50 <- sapply(S023Cxc, function(x) {
   HalfNumReads <- max(x$CumSum) / 2
   k <- min(which(x$CumSum >= HalfNumReads))

S117Cmb.N50 <- sapply(S117Cmb, function(x) {

S125Cmc.N50 <- sapply(S125Cmc, function(x) {
   HalfNumReads <- max(x$CumSum) / 2
   k <- min(which(x$CumSum >= HalfNumReads))
   N50 <- x[k, 'Size']
   return(N50)
})

N50 <- data.frame(
   Sample = rep(c('N044Cx2', 'S004Cmb', 'S023Cxc', 'S027Cxa',
                  'S117Cmb', 'S125Cma', 'S125Cmc'), each = 6),
   ClustThres = rep(c(0.85, 0.90, 0.92, 0.94, 0.96, 0.98), 7),
   N50 = c(N044Cx2.N50, S004Cmb.N50, S023Cxc.N50, S027Cxa.N50,
           S117Cmb.N50, S125Cma.N50, S125Cmc.N50)
)
```

N50 is the size (in number of reads) of the smallest size of the set of
largest clusters that contain half the total number of reads.

```{r thePlots}
paleta <- met.brewer('Hokusai1', 6)
plot(N044Cx2[[1]]$Size, N044Cx2[[1]]$Freq, type = 'l', col = paleta[1],
     xlab = 'Cluster size', ylab = 'Frequency', log = 'xy',
     main = 'N044Cx2', xlim = c(1, 100), lwd = 2)
lines(N044Cx2[[2]]$Size, N044Cx2[[2]]$Freq, col = paleta[2], lwd = 2)
lines(N044Cx2[[3]]$Size, N044Cx2[[3]]$Freq, col = paleta[3], lwd = 2)
lines(N044Cx2[[4]]$Size, N044Cx2[[4]]$Freq, col = paleta[4], lwd = 2)
lines(N044Cx2[[5]]$Size, N044Cx2[[5]]$Freq, col = paleta[5], lwd = 2)
lines(N044Cx2[[6]]$Size, N044Cx2[[6]]$Freq, col = paleta[6], lwd = 2)
legend(40, 20000, c(0.85, 0.90, 0.92, 0.94, 0.96, 0.98), col = paleta, lwd = 2)

ggplot(N50, aes(x = ClustThres, y = N50, color = Sample)) +
   geom_point() + geom_line() + xlab('Clustering threshold') +
   ylab('N50')
```

I expected a qualitative change in the way the number of clusters or their
average or median size covary with clustering thresholds. However, there is no
indication of any turning point, from which we could be merging paralogs or
splitting alleles. The only sensitive decision is to keep running the analysis
with more than one value and choose later. See @McCartney-Melstad2019.
